children: By Adriano Marchese and Megan Cheah

Tamarack Valley Energy agreed to acquire Headwater Exploration in an 10 billion Canadian dollars ($7.24 billion) all-stock deal, uniting two major operators to form a single heavy-oil producer in Alberta's Clearwater fairway.

The acquisition combines Headwater's low-cost production footprint with Tamarack's asset base, bringing together more than 1,500 sections of contiguous land across northern Alberta. Together, the companies are expected to deliver run-rate production of over 80,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day across their consolidated development areas, including Marten Hills, Nipisi, Marten Hills West, Pelican and Seal.
The companies said Tuesday that the merger will create the only publicly-traded pure-play Clearwater company and the larger producer in the area.
The move follows a broader consolidation wave across Western Canada as energy companies move to secure long-term drilling locations in oil-rich basins.

Recent mega transactions, such as Whitecap Resources' $10.44 billion combination with Veren in the Montney and Duvernay regions reflect an industry-wide push toward operational scale and infrastructure security.

Under the terms of the agreement, Headwater shareholders will receive one common share of Tamarack for each share held. Once the deal is closed, Tamarack shareholders will own about 66.5% of the combined entity, while Headwater shareholders will own the remaining 33.5%.

The combined business will be headed by Tamarack's executive team, with current president, Steve Buytels stepping into the chief executive role on Jan. 1, and founding CEO Brian Schmidt becoming executive chairman.
The combined business is expected to achieve over C$50 million in annual synergies, and to be immediately accretive to Tamarack's free funds flow per share.

The deal is also expected to enhance its five-year plan, positioning the combined company to deliver higher total shareholder returns, they said, including a proposed quarterly dividend hike of 20% once the deal closes.

Tamarack said that, following the merger, it will be able to accommodate the higher production volume with current and planned pipeline connections in the province. It said that it has secured 35,000 barrels a day of long-term export pipeline capacity out of Alberta, including 25,000 barrels a day on the Trans Mountain pipeline to the West Coast starting in early 2027, and 10,000 barrels a day on the proposed South Bow Prairie Connector to Oklahoma and the U.S. Gulf Coast later in 2028.
Certain noncore exploration assets will be transferred to a new exploration company, Tributary Exploration, which will be led by Headwater's current management team, the companies said.

The companies expect their 2026 capital program to range from C$450 million to C$470 million, reflecting incremental spending associated with Headwater's planned capital program and subject to the deal's completion. The companies' combined capital investment programs for the year are expected to total about C$700 million.
The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter following approvals at special meetings expected in November 2026, as well as court and regulatory clearances.
